summary: Shinjiro Kazama is a linguist who studied at Hokkaido University from around 1984 to 1992. He held a post at Tottori University from around 1997 to 2009 and became a professor at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies around 2009.

Shinjo Hinonishi was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied under Shigeru Gorai. He held academic posts at Koyasan University, serving as an assistant professor (attested 1980) and later as a professor (attested 2008).

Shinjo Kawasaki is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology who earned degrees at the University of Tokyo, studying under Hajime Nakamura and others. He served at the University of Tokyo, University at Buffalo, University of Tsukuba (1975–1997), and Taisho University.

Shinjo Suguro was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy who earned his degrees at the University of Tokyo. He was vice director at the Institute for the Comprehensive Study of the Lotus Sutra (1980) and professor at Rissho University (~1968–1996).
Shinjosei Mochizuki was a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Tokyo and Kyoto University, and later held a post at Tezukayama Gakuin University.
Shinkai Sugawara was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied at Waseda University and Taisho University. He served as professor emeritus at Waseda University.

Shinkan Murakami is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who earned doctorates at Tohoku University under Ensho Kanakura, Ryujo Yamada, and Hakuyu Hadano. He served as a professor at Tohoku University (~1974–1996) and held a post at Seiwa Gakuen College.

Shinko Nakai was a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology who studied at Kyoto Prefectural University. He served as a professor and university president at Bukkyo University from around 1972 to 2014, later becoming professor emeritus.

Shinkō Mochizuki studied under Tokuo Jonobe and completed degrees at Bukkyo, Taisho, and Tokyo universities. He held key posts at Taisho University (1926–1942), Shukyo University (1908–1928), and Chion-in Temple, and founded the Bussho Kankōkai and Mochizuki Institute of Buddhist Culture.
Shinobu Arai Apple is a scholar of Buddhist studies. She studied under Mark Csikszentmihalyi, Robert Bickner, and Charles Hallisey, who served as her doctoral supervisor (attested 2003).
Shinobu Yamaguchi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed a PhD at Nagoya University in 1995. She held an attested post as professor at Toyo University in 2015.

Shinsho Hanayama was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the Fourth Higher School and the University of Tokyo. He taught Buddhism at the University of Tokyo from around 1934 to 1959 and served as a professor at Toyo and Kokugakuin universities.

Shintaro Kitano is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Kazunobu Matsuda. He served as a researcher at Taisho University (attested 2005) and as a part-time lecturer at Kyushu University (attested 2015).
Shinten Sakai was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Shindo Shiraishi and held a post at Koyasan University (attested 1959).

Shinya Mano is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. He served as a part-time lecturer at Waseda University (attested 2015–2019) and as a research associate at SOAS University of London (attested 2019).

Shinya Moriyama is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Tokyo and completed his Dr.Phil at the University of Vienna under Eli Franco, later holding an academic post at Shinshu University around 2008.

Shiro Matsumoto is a Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology scholar who studied at Komazawa and Tokyo universities under Yasuaki Nara and Zuiho Yamaguchi. He held a professorship at Komazawa University (1995–2020) and visited Vienna (1987) and Chicago (2001).

Shiv Nath Sharma was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He held posts at the Jammu and Kashmir Research and Archaeological Department (attested 1947) and as a professor at St. Andrew's College, Gorakhpur (attested 1973).

Shiv Singh is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed a PhD at Gurukula Kangri Vishwavidyalaya between 2018 and 2024 and was appointed a postdoctoral researcher at the Indian Council of Social Science Research for 2026.

Shivram Dattatray Joshi was an Indologist and linguist who earned his doctorate at Harvard under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He served as professor and director at Savitribai Phule Pune University and headed Deccan College's Sanskrit Dictionary Department (1987–1997).
